newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss to give India bank secrets on Swedish arms deal.
newsitem.headline: Swiss to give India bank secrets on Swedish arms deal.

text.p: Switzerland will give India secret bank documents linked to a billion dollar arms scandal over Swedish artillery, justice officials said on Wednesday.
They said India's ambassador will receive the documents from the Federal Police Affairs Office, an agency of the justice ministry, in a public ceremony in Berne on January 21.
The hand-over will take place seven years after India first asked Switzerland for the documents and follows a final ruling by the Swiss supremwe court on November 26.
The high court overruled objections from a lower court in Geneva, including a decision last year that fair proceedings in India would be impossible.
The case stems from India's $1.3 billion artillery deal with Sweden's Bofors arms manufacturers in 1986.
India had been trying to discover whether leading Indian politicians took bribes in connection with the arms deal.
Following an Indian investigation which established that Bofors paid millions of dollars into Swiss bank accounts, Indian police asked Switzerland to provide details.
The furore contributed to the defeat in 1989 of the government led by late prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, who was accused by opposition parties of involvement in the affair.
Gandhi, who denied the allegations, was killed in a bomb blast while campaigning for 1991 parliamentary polls.
